policy: A divergence (a trait a platform genuinely cannot express) is only allowed with an explicit expiry date and an approver. No open-ended waivers. See .claude/skills/_guards/a11y-guard/SKILL.md.
note: Each entry authorizes the Lowering Ledger (_shared/scripts/ledger-gate.mjs) to accept a `diverged` trait. A ledger entry whose waiver id is absent, expired, or missing approver/expires FAILS the gate. Adding a trait a platform CAN express never belongs here — express it instead. Exception: a time-boxed waiver is allowed when its reason names a missing prerequisite (for example the a11y-labelledby-* waivers: id plumbing to the referenced element does not exist yet).

a11y-role-status.reason: role=status has no dedicated accessibilityRole (RN), accessibility trait (SwiftUI), or Compose Role. Conveyed via the accompanying live region (aria-live -> liveRegion), which carries the polite-announce semantics status implies. On SwiftUI no live trait is emitted (updatesFrequently does not announce, device-confirmed), so the role is conveyed by nothing until an imperative announcement capability exists; see docs/audits/F-28-value-lowering-audit.md. On React Native the live region (accessibilityLiveRegion) works on Android only (source-verified, not device-tested) and is inert on iOS (device-confirmed), so on iOS the role is conveyed by nothing until an imperative announcement capability exists.

a11y-role-alert.reason: role=alert has no SwiftUI trait or Compose Role. RN maps it to accessibilityRole="alert"; on Compose it is conveyed via the assertive/polite live region on the same node. On SwiftUI no live trait is emitted (updatesFrequently does not announce, device-confirmed), so the role is conveyed by nothing until an imperative announcement capability exists; see docs/audits/F-28-value-lowering-audit.md. On React Native the live region (accessibilityLiveRegion) works on Android only (source-verified, not device-tested) and is inert on iOS (device-confirmed), so on iOS the role is conveyed by nothing until an imperative announcement capability exists.

a11y-role-group.reason: role=group has no native accessibilityRole / SwiftUI trait / Compose Role. The grouping container still exposes its labelled children; the group boundary itself is a documented platform gap.

a11y-role-list.reason: role=list has no native accessibilityRole / SwiftUI trait / Compose Role. Native list semantics come from the platform's own list containers, not an ARIA role; the explicit role is a documented gap on a generic container.

a11y-role-listitem.reason: role=listitem has no native accessibilityRole / SwiftUI trait / Compose Role. Item membership is conveyed structurally by the list container; the explicit role is a documented gap.

a11y-role-separator.reason: role=separator has no native accessibilityRole / SwiftUI trait / Compose Role. The divider is decorative on native; its separating meaning is visual only, a documented gap.

a11y-describedby-native.reason: aria-describedby (an id reference to describing text) has no equivalent on React Native / SwiftUI / Compose, which have no cross-node id linkage. Conveyed via an adjacent live-region Text / accessibilityHint / stateDescription instead.

a11y-invalid-swiftui.reason: SwiftUI has no direct aria-invalid trait on a TextField/Toggle. The invalid state is conveyed by the adjacent error Text (itself a live region); a11y-invalid maps to aria-invalid on web/RN, so SwiftUI diverges.

a11y-invalid-compose.reason: A Compose Checkbox/Switch/Slider/RadioButton has no isError parameter (unlike a text field), so a11y-invalid on a non-text control has no direct trait. The invalid state is conveyed by the adjacent error Text (a live region); a11y-invalid maps to aria-invalid on web/RN, so this control diverges.

a11y-live-polite-swiftui.reason: a11y.live=polite on SwiftUI: there is no declarative live region API. The updatesFrequently trait only tells the system the element may be polled and, device-confirmed on a real iPhone with VoiceOver, it does NOT announce changes; only an imperative AccessibilityNotification.Announcement speaks (future capability, not implemented). Nothing is emitted for this value. See docs/audits/F-28-value-lowering-audit.md.

a11y-live-assertive-swiftui.reason: a11y.live=assertive on SwiftUI: there is no declarative live region API. The updatesFrequently trait only tells the system the element may be polled and, device-confirmed on a real iPhone with VoiceOver, it does NOT announce changes; only an imperative AccessibilityNotification.Announcement speaks (future capability, not implemented). Nothing is emitted for this value. See docs/audits/F-28-value-lowering-audit.md.

a11y-live-polite-react-native.reason: a11y.live=polite on React Native: accessibilityLiveRegion is tagged @platform android and has no iOS consumer (source-verified in react-native 0.87.1; device-confirmed inert on a real iPhone with VoiceOver). Android behaviour is source-verified only: TalkBack was NOT device-tested. The prop is emitted and is effective on Android only; an imperative AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility call for iOS is future work, not implemented. See docs/audits/F-28-value-lowering-audit.md.

a11y-live-assertive-react-native.reason: a11y.live=assertive on React Native: accessibilityLiveRegion is tagged @platform android and has no iOS consumer (source-verified in react-native 0.87.1; device-confirmed inert on a real iPhone with VoiceOver). Android behaviour is source-verified only: TalkBack was NOT device-tested. The prop is emitted and is effective on Android only; an imperative AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility call for iOS is future work, not implemented. See docs/audits/F-28-value-lowering-audit.md.

a11y-labelledby-react.reason: a11y.labelledBy on React: it needs a target element id, and the IR and adapters do not yet plumb ids to referenced elements, so emitting aria-labelledby now could point to nothing. Nothing is emitted until id plumbing exists. This is a time-boxed waiver for a missing prerequisite, not a platform limit; see docs/audits/F-28-value-lowering-audit.md.
